description: Archive kind 19, execution_result (core 19.2, since spec revision v1.1): one record per captured ordinary tx, key (chain_id, rail_ref), path exec/<chain_id>/<rail_ref hex>, identity the key. records: valid records and their keys, paths and the cause a v1.0 reader gives (it does not know kind 19). reject: must-reject records of a v1.1 reader (archive.ErrCorrupt with the cause). cases: the XR rules of core 20.2.2 on a record (base_record, then the change the description names) with the query (chain_id of the action, rail_ref of the receipt) and the hashes header trust reached (trusted, height -> hash); expect gives pass with the facts, or set_aside with the first failing rule and the reason of core 20.1.1. migration: a block file of the gate's capture store (the v1.0.4 JSON layout, byte strings in base64), the records the archive already holds under their paths (stored, optional), and what MG1 to MG7 (core 19.7) make of each captured tx: written (archived, capture entry dropped), already_stored (an equivalent record holds the key, by bytes or by facts; capture entry dropped) or refused/kept with the rule (capture entry stays). A case's rule decode is strict decoding through the verifier path (core 20.2.2). upstream: the synthetic blocks, built and checked with upstream code by spec/vectors/tools/execresult-gen; a block marked negative feeds failing cases only, and its captures are not in records.

inputs.pff_tx: the first PayForFibre unit of da/fibre_anchor.json live.cases[0].raw.namespace_data_hex
inputs.synthetic: every other tx, header field and result is fixed bytes (SHA-256 of a label), so a rebuild gives the same section

blocks.description: Two ordinary txs (the live bank-send tx first), a blob tx and the live PayForFibre tx: proofs of TX_NS, PFB_NS and PFF_NS plus the closing share.
One small ordinary tx in a 1 x 1 square: the transaction namespace ends the square, so there is no closing share.
One ordinary tx and one blob tx, no Fibre tx: proofs of TX_NS and PFB_NS plus the closing share; key 11 absent.
The same ordinary tx twice: two units of TX_NS hash to its rail_ref, so the record cannot bind the index (negative block).

Two ordinary txs in two TX_NS shares, with the sequence-start bit set on the second share after Construct: the namespace holds a second sequence start (negative block, a layout go-square never builds).

A forgery of block three_namespaces: same chain id and height, the live bank-send tx alone with result code 13, fabricated headers that link to each other. Self-consistent, so it passes the gate's self-check without a trust root (MG3), but not the trusted chain (negative block; the migration's squatted key).

reject.description: Key 16 is not defined for kind 19.
Key 15 (result_path) is required, even when empty.
rail_ref is a bstr, not the hex text of the receipt.
chain_id starting with a dot (a dot file in the canonical path).
An optional proof present but empty.

cases.description: The live bank-send tx at index 0 of a block with all three transaction namespaces and the closing share: inclusion and result proven, code 0 (outcome success).
Index 1 of the same block, code 5: the result is proven, outcome failure (the profile's BX9 then gives fail, bank-send ErrTxFailed).
A 1 x 1 square: the transaction namespace ends the square, no closing proof, an empty result path (results_total 1).
TX_NS and PFB_NS, then the closing share; key 11 absent.
The record read for another rail_ref (stored under the wrong key).
Header trust reaches the height but not height + 1.
The trusted chain has another header at the height.
Cross-chain substitution: the record's key names chain arabica-11 (and the verifier asks for it), but both headers are of mocha-5.
The record names height + 1; its header is the header at height.
The trusted header at the height has app version 9: the ordering rule is pinned to app version 10.
The closing proof is the PFB_NS proof: its namespace does not follow PFF_NS.
Key 10 holds the PFF_NS proof: its namespace is not PFB_NS.

Key 10 holds the PFB_NS proof of block tx_then_blob (square width 2, the record's square is 8 wide): it does not reach data_hash. The check that every proof has the same width is a second line behind this one, because a row proof of another width cannot reach the same data_hash.
One byte of a row root of the TX_NS proof changed: the row proof does not reach data_hash.
The PFB_NS proof is missing: the PFF_NS range does not start where TX_NS ends.
The closing proof is missing and the transaction namespaces do not end the square.
Key 9 proves TX_NS share 1 only (a valid proof of a sub-range): it does not start at share 0.
Key 9 proves TX_NS share 0 only: the sequence length needs two shares, so the key does not hold one whole compact sequence.
The closing proof covers two shares of the blob after PFB_NS.
TX_NS holds a second sequence start inside key 9 (a square go-square never builds; the block is on its own trusted chain here).
results_total 3 instead of 4. The RFC 6962 path alone still verifies (index 0 of 3 and of 4 have the same shape), so only the count of the complete transaction namespaces catches it.
tx_index 1 for the tx at unit 0 of TX_NS.
A rail_ref that no ordinary tx of the block hashes to, read under that key.
Two units of TX_NS hash to rail_ref: the index is not bound (which of the two results is the receipt's transaction is unknown).
The result leaf carries field 3 (log), which the results hash does not cover.
One byte of the result path changed.
The failed tx at index 1 presented with code 0: the root does not match.
The record read through the verifier path fails strict decoding (key 16): set aside before any XR rule.
